questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

Just punishment for wrong doing
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘Nemesis’**

**Nemesis **means **‘a downfall caused by an inescapable agent.’**

Hence, it is the closest in meaning to the given phrase and is the correct one-word substitute.

The other options,

Dandy means ‘excellent’

Prodigy means ‘an outstanding example of a particular quality’

Wagon means ‘a vehicle used for transporting or another purpose’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

The kids were laughing at the old lady.

options.text: The old lady is laughing at the kids.
The old lady was being laughed at by the kids.
The old lady was being laughed by the kids.
The old lady was laughed at by the kids.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘The old lady was being laughed at by the kids.’**

Sentence 1 changes the meaning completely and is incorrect.

Sentence 3 removes ‘at’ and thus, the meaning changes, making the sentence incorrect in the Passive voice.

Sentence 4 changes the tense and removes the continuous part (laughing), making it incorrect.

Only **Sentence 2** retains the meaning the sentence and accurately converts the Active voice to the Passive voice.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P- In that frame of mind, we have little sense of identity, safety or security.

Q- Courage is required to explore our secret life because we must first withdraw from the social mirror, where we are fed positive and negative feedback continuously.

S- As we get used to this social feedback, it becomes a comfort zone.

R- And we may opt to avoid self examination and idle away our time in a vacuum of reverie and rationalization.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘QSRP’**

The first sentence is Q, as it introduces ‘courage’.

It is followed by S, as it follows on the ‘feedback’ chain.

Then comes by R, followed by P, which talk about the ‘comfort zone’ and ‘frame of mind’.

Hence, the correct combination is QSRP, as seen in **Option 1.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

"Do you want some more chocolates?" asked my cousin.

options.text: My cousin asked me if I want some more chocolates.
My cousin said to me if I wanted some more chocolates.
My cousin asked me that I wanted some more chocolates.
My cousin asked me whether I wanted some more chocolates.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘My cousin asked me whether I wanted some more chocolates.’**

Sentence 1 does not convert to the past tense in the reported speech and is incorrect.

Sentence 2 uses an incorrect reporting verb, ‘said to’, instead of ‘asked’. 

Sentence 3 is incorrect in structure (asked…that) and is rejected.

Only **Sentence 4** uses the correct reporting verb and tense and is the correct conversion from Direct to Indirect speech.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

My brother finds it difficult (1)/ to pass away the time (2)/ at our grandparent's house. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in **Part 2** of the sentence.

**‘Pass away’** means ‘to cease or die’.

The correct word to be used in the sentence is **pass**, which means ‘spend or live’.

Hence, the correct sentence is:

**‘My brother finds it difficult to pass the time at our grandparent’s house.’**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P- To those who have known comfort, discomfort is a real torture.

Q- Comfort is now one of the causes of its own spread.

R- The more comfort is brought into the world, the more it is likely to be valued.

S- It has now become a physical habit, a fashion, an ideal to be pursued for its own sake.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘QSRP’.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
 
• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• Part Q will be the first sentence because it introduces the topic 'comfort'.
 
• **Part S **mentions how comfort is turning into a habit and states the reason for comfort as one of the reasons for its spread.
 
• **Part R **will be the next in sequence. Its mentions how comfort is turning valuable.
 
• **Part P **mentions discomfort is the real torture for those who have taken comfort as a habit​__

__Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *Comfort is now one of the causes of its own spread. It has now become a physical habit, a fashion, an ideal to be pursued for its own sake. The more comfort is brought into the world, the more it is likely to be valued. To those who have known comfort, discomfort is a real torture.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the paragraph.
 
• Try to identify the opening and closing sentences of the paragraph. The sentence independent of the other sentences and introduces the new characters is generally the opening sentence. For the last sentence, look out for the sentence which can conclude the paragraph.
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
 
• Identify the pronouns which are connecting the sentences with each other.
 
• Sometimes it is not necessary to identify all the sentences, we can arrange the sentences by eliminating the irrelevant option one by one.
